correctness.rationale: For all integers n>=2 and real s>=1/2, the transport norm is 1/2 sum |x_i|+(s-1/2)|sum x_i|; reverse dual potentials use levels s and s-1, valid under the metric triangle bound. The polar range constraint |f_i|<=s, |f_i-f_j|<=1 gives volume 2ns-n+1 by integrating range r<=1. Splitting primal coordinates by signs, integrating positive and negative totals and applying Vandermonde gives 2/(n!s^n) sum_{j=0}^{n-1} binom(n-1+j,j)s^j. Differentiation factors as 2(1-s)/(n!s^(n+1)) times a polynomial with all positive coefficients, hence the strict equilateral maximum at s=1 and both endpoint identities. Independently checked symbolic derivative identities for n=2..11 using SymPy and inspected exact-orthant/hull reproducer. The polynomial proof, not the finite n test, establishes universal quantifiers.
residual_risks: Finite verification does not prove all quantified real/dimensional claims; the proof was independently reconstructed and checked against boundary cases.
